Ramil Khafizov

I’m a PhD researcher at the Applied AI Institute, working on generative AI and visual foundation models. I study efficient and controllable generation through diffusion, flow matching, and autoregression, and I’m interested in world models.

I develop models and training pipelines end to end, with experiments on models up to 2B parameters and multi-node setups of up to 32 H100 GPUs. Previously, I was a deep learning researcher at Artec 3D, where I worked on generative 3D editing, spatial vision-language modeling, and promptable 3D segmentation.

Input Generated

NAMVIS: Next-Scale Autoregressive Multi-View Image Synthesis

Ramil Khafizov, Ilya Statsenko, Ruslan Rakhimov, Artem Komarichev, Peter Wonka, Evgeny Burnaev

NeurIPS, 2026

project page / paper / code / bibtex

I led end-to-end model development and training, including multi-scale camera conditioning for consistent novel-view generation. NAMVIS uses next-scale autoregression without iterative denoising and runs over 3× faster than the evaluated diffusion baselines.

One Algorithm to Align Them All

Boyi Pang, Savva Ignatyev, Vladimir Ippolitov, Ramil Khafizov, Yurii Melnik, Oleg Voynov, Maksim Nakhodnov, Aibek Alanov, Xiaopeng Fan, Peter Wonka, Evgeny Burnaev

CVPR, 2026

project page / paper / arXiv / bibtex

A training-free rectified-flow method for jointly generating structurally aligned images, videos, and 3D shapes.

3D reconstruction

G-CUT3R: Guided 3D Reconstruction with Camera and Depth Prior Integration

Ramil Khafizov, Artem Komarichev, Ruslan Rakhimov, Peter Wonka, Evgeny Burnaev

arXiv preprint, 2025

paper / code / bibtex

Feed-forward 3D reconstruction that incorporates available depth, camera calibration, and pose priors through modality-specific encoders and zero-initialized fusion.

Ongoing research

ARGeoSplat: Autoregressive Geometry Generation and Refinement for Sparse-View 3D Reconstruction

Ramil Khafizov, Artem Komarichev, Ilya Statsenko, Ruslan Rakhimov, Peter Wonka, Evgeny Burnaev

Submitted to ICLR, 2027

Joint next-scale autoregressive generation of RGB views and quantized 3D pointmaps, with geometry supervision and cost-volume depth refinement for sparse-view 3D Gaussian reconstruction.

Open source

Shortcut Models — PyTorch reproduction

My independent implementation, training, and open-source release of Shortcut Models for one- and few-step flow-matching generation. Code & results.
